source: Alpaca paper account activity, PA3LY20ABUNE, supplied by the owner
what_this_is: The first regulatory fees this project has ever observed. One completed round trip, and the fee formulas are checked against the regulators' own published rates rather than estimated from it.
why_one_observation_is_enough: Section 31 and TAF are deterministic functions of proceeds and shares. One observation CHECKS a formula. It would estimate nothing about a distribution, which is why the same sample says nothing about slippage.

section_31.rate: 20.60 USD per 1,000,000 USD of covered sales

finra_taf.per_trade_maximum: 8.30 USD as the rule text reads; FINRA is phasing in increases during 2026 and a 5.95 figure also appears. NOT ESTABLISHED, and immaterial at this size.

cat.why: 0.01 on one trade and 0.01 on twelve. Not linear in trades, so neither observation constrains a per-trade rate.

verification.method: predicted from the published rate, rounded UP to the cent, compared to the billed amount
verification.rounding_is_INFERRED_not_published: Both amounts match under round-up-to-the-cent and neither matches under round-half. Two independent confirmations of the same rule, which is evidence about Alpaca's implementation rather than a published fact.

materiality.note: DR-004 charges 3.4x the entire real fee bill, for a commission this venue does not charge. The regulatory fees are 0.9% of the slippage term and will not move any verdict.

not_established: Whether a paper account is billed the same schedule as a live one.
The TAF per-trade maximum during the 2026 phase-in.
Whether Alpaca's round-up is a policy or an artefact of these two amounts.
